title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: choose file extensions from a curated list
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, existing-policy behaviour and licensing are supported, including by the changed Purview service description. Two minor corrections remain: complete the replacement-control path and remove the inventory checklist instruction that has no controls-table row.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP is replacing free-text file-extension configuration with a curated picker.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP now includes a pre curated list of file extensions for the file extension condition.

claims.claim: File extensions were previously entered as free-form text.
claims.quote: Previously, file extensions were entered as free form text

claims.claim: The roadmap says unsupported or non-scannable extensions could leave gaps in protection.
claims.quote: which could result in unsupported or non-scannable extensions being used. This could lead to gaps in protection

claims.claim: The roadmap says the curated list reduces unnecessary endpoint processing.
claims.quote: This helps improve policy reliability and reduces unnecessary processing on endpoints.

claims.claim: Only supported, scannable file types appear in the picker.
claims.quote: Only file types that are supported and can be scanned appear in the picker.

claims.claim: Free-form extension entry is no longer available once the change rolls out.
claims.quote: Free‑form text entry for file extensions is no longer available.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing policies keep enforcing as today unless edited.
claims.quote: Existing policies continue to enforce as they do today unless edited.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An edited policy containing unsupported extensions cannot be saved until those entries are removed.
claims.quote: If an edited policy contains unsupported file extensions, those entries must be removed before the policy can be saved.

claims.quote: To maintain coverage for unsupported or non‑scannable file types, use the Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions feature.

claims.quote: In contrast, the **Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions** feature does not scan file content.

claims.claim: The picker is on by default in the sense that it replaces free-form entry on rollout without an enablement step.
claims.quote: Free‑form text entry for file extensions is no longer available. ... No action required if you are not modifying existing policies.

claims.claim: The roadmap and supplied notice describe no change to roles, identities or permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: supplied roadmap description and full MC1384415 for changes to roles, identities and permissions; neither specifies any. The notice identifies the affected administrators without changing their permissions.

claims.claim: The notice does not describe existing block, warn or audit settings as changing.
claims.quote: Searched: full MC1384415 What will happen and Action Required for changes to rule actions; it changes extension selection and saving, and says existing policies continue to enforce as today unless edited.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn warns that blocking extensions such as .dll, .json and .tmp can disrupt unallowed applications that need those files.
claims.quote: certain apps might read or temporarily open files, like `.dll`, `.json`, `.tmp` during routine processes such as rendering, caching, or validating content. If you block these extensions, the app might fail to function properly

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence or meter specific to the curated picker is published in the checked sources.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP file extension licensing meter; read Purview service description, Endpoint DLP getting-started, roadmap and MC1384415. The service table includes Endpoint DLP; none names a picker-specific licence or meter.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no numerical figure for its claimed processing reduction.
claims.quote: This helps improve policy reliability and reduces unnecessary processing on endpoints.

claims.claim: The notice identifies Microsoft 365 administrators managing Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP device policies as affected.
claims.quote:
Who is affected:

  - Microsoft 365 administrators managing Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP device policies.

claims.claim: The notice's platform/service list names Microsoft Purview, Endpoint DLP and supported Windows endpoints.
claims.quote:
Platforms/Services:

  - Microsoft Purview

claims.claim: No additional picker-specific prerequisites are stated in the checked sources.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP curated prerequisites; read MC1384415, roadmap, endpoint-dlp-getting-started and dlp-policy-reference. No picker-specific prerequisite is stated; general Endpoint DLP requirements remain.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing current file-extension lists when planning policy creation or edits.
claims.quote:
If you plan to edit or create a policy:
    
      - Review your current file extension list.

claims.claim: Learn cautions administrators to test unsupported-file policies outside production.
claims.quote: Test this policy in a nonproduction environment before deploying it to your production environment.

claims.claim: No tenant UI or API switch to retain free-form entry or disable the curated picker is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP curated disable; Endpoint DLP curated PowerShell. Read endpoint-settings, policy-reference, New-DlpComplianceRule and Set-PolicyConfig search excerpts. No picker opt-out is documented; MC1384415 says free-form entry is no longer available.

claims.claim: The cited Microsoft Purview portal route starts Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Enterprise applications & devices > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy.
claims.quote:
Open **Data Loss Prevention** > **Policies**.
3. Select **Enterprise applications & devices**.
4. Select **Create policy** and select the **Custom** from the **Categories** then **Custom policy** template from **Regulations**.
claims.fix: Complete the path as 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Enterprise applications & devices > Create policy > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom policy > Admin units > Full directory > Devices > rule > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions', retaining Document could not be scanned in the note. This follows https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-files-edlp-doesnt-scan. Note that the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-sharing-set-unsupported-files instead puts Create policy before Enterprise applications & devices.

claims.claim: No documented automation call was found that specifically configures Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Apply restrictions to only unsupported file extensions" "PowerShell"; "EndpointDlpRestrictions" "unsupported". Read New-DlpComplianceRule parameters and Set-DlpComplianceRule/Set-PolicyConfig excerpts; no deciding setting for this option is specified.

claims.claim: The cited replacement-policy procedure uses Full directory, Devices and Document could not be scanned before configuring the device restriction action.
claims.quote:
Select **Full directory** under **Admin units**.
7. Scope the location to **Devices** only.
8. Create a rule where:
    1. In **Conditions**:
        1. Select **Document could not be scanned**.

claims.claim: The replacement policy is configured at tenant level with Full directory administrative scope.
claims.quote: Administrative scope: **Full directory**

claims.claim: Unsupported file extension exclusions is a separate Endpoint DLP setting that narrows unsupported-file coverage.
claims.quote: Because this condition can potentially include many unsupported file extensions, refine detection by adding unsupported extensions to exclude.
